classification.difficultyReason: Combine vectors, calculate an exact magnitude and interpret a fourth-quadrant direction.

content.prompt:
Find the magnitude and direction of $\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y}$ given that $\underset{\sim}{x}=5\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{y}=-2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}$.

Give magnitude in exact form and direction to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y}&=(5\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})+(-2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})=3\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}\\ \left|\underset{\sim}{x}+\underset{\sim}{y}\right|&=\sqrt{3^2+(-2)^2}=\sqrt{9+4}=\sqrt{13}\\ \tan\theta&=-\frac{2}{3}\\ \theta&=\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\approx-33.7^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The vector is in the fourth quadrant.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Direction}&=360^\circ-33.7^\circ\\ &\approx326^\circ\end{aligned}$$
